summary: Atsushi Uno worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under Raghunath Giri, T. R. V. Murti, and others. He held posts at Shuchiin, Tokai, Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (attested 1988–1989) universities.

Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Doshisha and Kyoto universities, where he learned under Ryosaburo Sakaki and later served as professor and director, alongside positions at Tokai University and the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan.
Atsuyoshi Keika works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University, attested as lecturer in 1990 and as professor in 2014.

August Boeckh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher, and held posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, earning degrees at Würzburg and Leipzig. He spent most of his academic career at Leipzig University, becoming full professor of Sinology in 1920, and held a post at Peking University (1903–1904).

August Dillmann worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald and held academic posts at Tübingen, Kiel, Giessen, and Frederick William University Berlin (1869–1894).
August Ferdinand Naeke studied at Leipzig University from 1806 to 1810. He held academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and at the University of Bonn (1818–1838).

August Fick was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He later served as professor of comparative linguistics at Göttingen (1876) and as ordinary professor at Breslau (1887–1891).

August Fischer worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1884–1889) and later held posts at Leipzig University (1900–1930) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

August Friedrich Pott specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Göttingen and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He lectured at Humboldt University of Berlin before becoming professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle from 1833.

August Hermann Francke worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Lehrerseminar in Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he became a Privatdozent in 1922.

August Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Gothenburg, and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

August Johan Bernet Kempers specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Leiden University. He served as director of Dinas Purbakala (1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien was a linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as professor at Jena and Göttingen before his long professorship at Leipzig University from 1870 to 1915.
August Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as director of Aliah University (1881–1899) and was secretary of The Asiatic Society in 1891.

August Schleicher was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others, later serving as professor at Charles University (1850–1857) and the University of Jena (1857).

August Wilhelm Schlegel worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Gottfried August Bürger, and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy and Alexander Hamilton, later holding professorships at Jena, Breslau, and Bonn.

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his licence at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at Collège de Saverne (1860–1870) and was a member of the Institut de France.
Auguste Comte was a philosopher who completed his education in France, studying at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and then at École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.
Aung San Suu Kyi studied in Tibetology and other fields at Lady Shri Ram College, the University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS. She held a post at the United Nations from 1969 to 1971.
